The company did not reveal specific platform functionalities or intended users, provided no details on expected profitability, payment milestones, or projected revenue contribution, and confirmed it had received only an order rather than completed delivery.
items.title: RailTel Secures ₹27.03 Crore AI Legal Assistant Contract From Andhra Pradesh

items.summary:
According to a Wall Street Journal report, 52-year-old Chinese national Li Ming, who faces fraud charges in Singapore over the alleged transshipment of servers equipped with Nvidia chips, played a central role in a network that supplied advanced computing capacity to Chinese customers. Prosecutors allege that Li purchased computer servers fitted with Nvidia chips and misled an American supplier by claiming the equipment was destined for his Singapore-based company; prosecutors say the servers were instead routed through Malaysia to an unidentified third destination. Although Megaspeed—a company where Alice Huang, identified as former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's romantic partner, served as managing director—was central to Li's activities, it was not among the companies named in the charges filed in February 2025.

Corporate registry records cited by the newspaper show that Alice Huang and her husband Kang Wei established a cloud-computing joint venture called Century Longteng in 2021. A January 2023 social media photograph described Li as Century Longteng's chief strategy officer, though his lawyers declined to comment on this characterization.

The three reportedly built a network of Southeast Asian partners providing computing capacity to Chinese customers and acquired the Singapore unit of a Chinese video game company, renaming it Megaspeed. After telling Nvidia that Alibaba was an anchor customer, Megaspeed joined the chipmaker's cloud partner programme in November 2023, gaining priority access to purchase the latest chips; prosecutors allege Megaspeed then routed servers through Malaysia to provide legal offshore computing capacity to Alibaba before some were sent to Shanghai-based Century Litong in violation of US export controls. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on an internal "no sell" list in June 2025, around the time of the investigations.

Megaspeed maintains it conducts legitimate business and said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025; Singapore officials questioned her over chip-smuggling suspicions but allowed her to leave while barring re-entry. The team reportedly launched a new venture called Novagate Cloud, which shipment records reviewed by the newspaper show received at least USD 300 million worth of Nvidia-chip hardware at one Malaysian entity during the first five months of 2026.

The report notes several limitations: all claims are attributed to WSJ reporting citing unnamed sources and corporate registry records rather than confirmed facts; Li's lawyers, Megaspeed, Century Litong, and Century Longteng declined or failed to comment; Nvidia placed Megaspeed on a "no sell" list but did not confirm wrongdoing; and the connection between Novagate and Megaspeed rests partly on a May Culper Research short-selling report citing near-identical websites and shared addresses rather than direct evidence. The WSJ also noted that Alice Huang, Kang Wei, and several other companies could not be reached for comment.
items.title: Singapore Fraud Charges Link Chinese National Li Ming To Nvidia Chip-Supply Network

items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed admiration for ancient Indian culture during a conversation with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, describing the country as home to one of the oldest civilisations. He characterised India's linguistic diversity as "stunning" and noted that many people speak Hindi, the nation's official language. The remarks were reported by Vijaya Srivastava, a journalist who focuses on society, healthcare, public policy, and emerging trends. The source text provides no additional context regarding when or where this conversation took place.
items.title: Putin Praises India's Linguistic Diversity and Ancient Civilisation

items.summary: The BJP on Sunday criticized Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of harbouring an "inherent hate for Sanatan" in response to his remarks about the party and RSS. The dispute arose after Gandhi posted a Shiva-Parvati sculpture image while describing the BJP and RSS as "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists" who lack understanding of India's spiritual and religious traditions. BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari cited earlier comments in which Gandhi referred to Sanatan Dharma as "dengue, malaria," framing these statements together as evidence of hostility toward the tradition. Kangana Ranaut, an actor and BJP MP, separately accused Congress of opposing women's reservation. The report is attributed to Aastha Jha, a writer at The Times of India covering politics; it presents the BJP's characterization of Gandhi's remarks without independently verifying his statements or intent.
items.title: BJP Accuses Rahul Gandhi of 'Inherent Hate for Sanatan' Over Religious Remarks

items.summary: Negotiations at COP31 concluded without a main agreement, known as a cover decision, after discussions over explicitly including fossil fuels and related issues proved irreconcilable. The talks continued past the failure on the cover decision, having made progress on smaller issues that touched both the process and the warming problem. Because any pact requires near-unanimous consensus, several countries and the 27-nation European Union declined to accept the final proposal from joint Turkish-Australian leadership because it omitted fossil fuels; Russia and Saudi Arabia pushed to keep such language out of the document. A larger number of nations accepted a decision that prioritized reaching some form of consensus over content, often reluctantly. Compounding disagreement was draft language setting an explicit goal for carbon capture and storage among industrial polluters, which many nations and activists said could undermine broader emission-reduction efforts. Union of Concerned Scientists' Rachel Cleetus attributed the failure to richer nations, petrostates, and what she called a 'disgracefully incompetent duo' of Turkish and Australian COP presidents. During the plenary session collapse, Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum was absent, leaving Azerbaijan's Elchin Allahverdiyev to announce the outcome; Australia's Chris Bowen described it as disappointing but affirmed that transition away from coal, oil, and natural gas remains in force regardless of the deal.
items.title: COP31 Fails to Reach a Cover Decision Over Fossil Fuel Language

items.summary: Rajasthan's Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has registered an FIR alleging that senior IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal misused his official position to benefit Goyal Fashions Pvt Ltd—the company operating resorts under the Ananta brand—in return for financial benefits to himself and his family. The ACB alleges the family acquired 64 villas and cottages from the resort company over roughly two-and-a-half years, including a recent batch of 24 Jaipur properties bought by Agrawal's sons at ₹11 lakh each versus an advertised brochure price of about ₹59 lakh per unit—a difference the ACB cites as approximately 81%. The FIR names Agrawal along with Goyal Fashions directors Mukund Saran Goyal and Sanjay Goyal, and examines official decisions spanning 2006 to 2026 across his tenures as Udaipur district collector, chairman of the Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board, and additional chief secretary of the Industries Department. The investigation also scrutinizes a revised Consent to Establish/Operate checklist adopted by the pollution board on August 28, 2023, which removed land conversion document requirements; it alleges Agrawal approved CTE for Ananta resorts at Ajabgarh (December 12, 2023) and Damodara Jaisalmer (June 7, 2024), with the former reportedly located near Sariska Tiger Reserve. The ACB's allegations remain under investigation and have not been established by a court; Agrawal and IPS officer Prashakha Mathur were placed on Awaiting Posting Orders amid the case, though the Rajasthan High Court declined to grant interim protection or halt the probe. No chart was identified as useful for this text, so visual is null.
items.title: Rajasthan ACB registers FIR against IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal over alleged discounted property deals and environmental approvals

items.summary:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi compared citizens holding off on non-essential gold purchases to former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri's 1965 wartime appeal for people to skip a meal. Speaking in Lucknow, Modi thanked the public for reducing gold buying, which he said helped conserve foreign exchange amid rising crude oil prices and contributed to lower gold rates.

The Chamber of Trade and Industry supported the move, noting it saved jewellers significant losses, while Union Minister Piyush Goyal defended the remarks by citing effects on global bullion prices. The BJP argued that the restraint protected traders and conserved foreign exchange.

Opposition Congress spokespersons criticized Modi's comparison as part of a broader debate over his appeal to curb non-essential gold imports and its economic impact.
items.title: Modi Compares Gold Purchase Restraint to Shastri's Wartime Austerity Appeal

items.summary: A debate between BJP's Sanju Verma and Congress' Brijesh Kalappa centered on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's request to limit non-essential gold purchases. Verma defended the move, arguing it would help conserve foreign exchange reserves and reduce both trade and current account deficits. In response, Kalappa questioned the comparison to Lal Bahadur Shastri's austerity measures and urged the government to focus instead on controlling inflation in essential goods such as fuel, pulses, and cooking oil. The source text presents these positions without independent verification of their accuracy or completeness. Additional unrelated items appear alongside this debate—including a Tamil Nadu Supreme Court review request regarding Karthigai Deepam lighting at Thiruparankundram hill, BJP president Nitin Nabin's claims that Rahul Gandhi evades parliamentary debates and follows foreign directives while praising Modi—none of which are substantiated beyond the source's assertions. The text also references an unverified political-culinary dispute over biryani preferences ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh elections.
items.title: BJP and Congress Leaders Clash Over Modi's Call to Limit Non-Essential Gold Imports

items.summary:
On Saturday, cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and was appointed a special invitee to the party's Other Backward Classes (OBC) wing representing Delhi. The appointment was announced by BJP leader Amar Pal Maurya on social media following a meeting between Chahal and Maurya in Delhi, as reported by The Indian Express; during that meeting, Maurya said Chahal had shown interest in politics and expressed a desire to work with the party. In a separate post, Chahal thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, and Maurya for their support.

The political move comes after Chahal announced his retirement from first-class cricket on October 2; he continues playing limited-overs formats, including One Day Internationals, Twenty20 Internationals, and the Indian Premier League. The report is attributed to Anamika Pathak with editing by Sara Varghese.
items.title: Cricket Spin Bowler Yuzvendra Chahal Joins BJP and Is Appointed to Its OBC Wing

items.summary: A wedding in Sonipat, Haryana was cancelled on Saturday when the groom, identified as Delhi police constable Kuldeep, reportedly refused to proceed with his marriage to 20-year-old Heena over an alleged demand for a more expensive dowry vehicle. The incident occurred at Mamchand Vatika after the groom arrived early Saturday evening with his mother and left the venue following a confrontation in which he allegedly abused relatives of the bride's family. According to Subhash Kumar, the bride's father, the alliance had been finalized around six months ago and the groom's family initially agreed to accept a Hyundai Aura worth approximately ₹9.5 lakh; the groom later insisted on a Maruti Brezza valued at roughly ₹13 lakh. The bride's family stated it had already arranged the Aura but could not meet the revised demand at short notice, and that additional demands for jewellery were also raised after finalization. The couple had spent money arranging furniture, electronic goods, household items, booking a banquet hall, and organizing food for around 1,200 guests. When questioned about his decision, the groom reportedly refused to proceed with the marriage, leaving the family embarrassed in front of relatives and guests; both families subsequently contacted police helpline 112, after which Subhash Kumar filed a written complaint at Sector 27 police station seeking action against the groom and his relatives and reimbursement of wedding expenses. DCP (Crime) Jitender Gehlawat said a panchayat meeting was underway to resolve the matter through mediation while an investigation continued into the exact cause of the dispute, with further legal action pending after the meeting.
items.title: Sonipat wedding called off after Delhi police constable allegedly demanded a costlier dowry car

items.summary: Ribha Lama, also known as Riva, a close aide of Darjeeling BJP MLA Noman Rai, was arrested on Saturday (November 21) during a police raid at a shopping mall in Matigara, Siliguri. He is accused of cheating brothers Shubhankar Arora and Dipankar Arora (alias Manik), who filed a written complaint with the Siliguri police on November 18 after Lama allegedly took money from them in several instalments during 2024 while promising to help them secure work contracts under the Sevoke-Rangpo railway project. The brothers reported paying more than Rs 1 crore across these instalments and receiving neither the promised employment nor a refund, prompting police to launch an investigation into both the financial transactions and whether Lama had any actual connection with the railway project. Sources indicated that Rai was present at the mall when police arrived but has not been named in the complaint, carries no allegation of involvement in the alleged fraud, and had issued no public statement on his aide's arrest as of report filing. The Trinamool Congress criticized the BJP over the allegations involving the MLA's associate while police continue their investigation.
items.title: Aide of Darjeeling BJP MLA Noman Rai arrested in Siliguri over alleged Rs 1-crore railway contract fraud

items.summary: A Hindustan Times newsdesk roundup dated Sunday, November 22, recaps the day's top headlines from India, the world, sports, and entertainment. The briefing leads with Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah arriving in India on Sunday evening for his first visit since taking office in March; he is scheduled to hold bilateral talks with PM Narendra Modi on Monday, November 23, alongside meetings with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and President Droupadi Murmu, accompanied by senior officials. Separately, seven people—including two serving Indian Army personnel, their wives, and three children from Uttarakhand's Garhwal region—died when a Hyundai Aura collided with a truck on the Bhuj-Khavda highway in Gujarat's Kutch district between 9:30 pm and 10 pm; PM Modi announced compensation of ₹2 lakh per deceased family member and ₹50,000 for each injured person from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund. In cricket, India posted a first-innings lead of 352 runs (720 total) in the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve, entering Day 4 with a 233-run lead and eight wickets remaining; Jasprit Bumrah dismissed Tom Latham for a second-ball duck while Rachin Ravindra joined Devon Conway to build an unbeaten third-wicket partnership of 59 runs as New Zealand reached 119/2 at close. On climate diplomacy, COP31 talks in Turkey reached an impasse when presidents of Turkey and Australia failed to secure consensus, with the EU rejecting a final draft deal that omitted mention of fossil fuels; Reuters cited EU delegation spokesman Ireland minister Darragh O'Brien stating they would not endorse a cover decision or Antalya pact failing to address fossil fuels. The entertainment item notes Ajay Devgn's Drishyam: The Conclusion will stream on Netflix on November 27 after earning ₹589 crore worldwide, following its October 2 theatrical release.
items.title: HT Evening News Brief (November 22): Nepal PM's India Visit, COP31 Deadlock, and India-New Zealand Test

items.summary: A review of Sabahattin Ali's novella Madonna in a Fur Coat reports that the work, first published in serial form in the Turkish daily Hakikat between 1941 and 1942, has gained sudden popularity among young adult readers following its 2021 edition. The English translation by Maureen Freely and Alexander Dawe was released in 2016; the review attributes the book's earlier obscurity to minimal early reader response but frames the recent surge as comparable to revivals of Dostoevsky's White Nights and Benedetti's The Truce, all united thematically around doomed love. Plot details drawn from the text describe a middle-aged narrator who learns about his colleague Raif Efendi through his private notebooks, revealing a shy 24-year-old man sent to Berlin for soapmaking training who becomes infatuated with a painting titled 'Maria Puder, Selbsporträt' and subsequently meets its subject, Maria, a cabaret singer whose forthright behavior reverses traditional gender roles as she repeatedly declines monogamy. The review characterizes the relationship as marked by sorrow rather than youthful playfulness, notes Raif's cultural bewilderment and views that border on misogyny while declining to label the novel sexist, and highlights practical interruptions involving visa limitations and family obligations in Turkey—framed as a contemporary concern about increasingly impenetrable borders. The reviewer connects the book's renewed appeal partly to modern social conditions including hostile nation-states and unstable gender roles, but offers this as speculation rather than established fact; the review also notes that Ali himself lived briefly in Berlin near a Maria Puder before dying tragically in Turkey, though it does not establish how these biographical details influenced the text. The account presents these observations without independent verification of claims about reader demographics or sales figures beyond the stated editions and reissues.
items.title: Rediscovered 1943 Novella 'Madonna in a Fur Coat' Draws Young Adult Readers

items.summary: As the United States tightened visa scrutiny and IT job uncertainty grew, students from Andhra Pradesh and Telangana increasingly turned away from American master's programmes toward European alternatives. Overseas education consultant N Ramana Rao attributed a decline of nearly 60 to 70 per cent in US-bound students from these states to Section 214(b) refusals at the Hyderabad Consulate, stricter social media screening, and longer interview waits of about 45 to 50 days. The shift is reflected in cost comparisons: an 18- to 24-month US master's totals roughly Rs 60 lakh to Rs 90 lakh (tuition Rs 20-35 lakh plus living costs Rs 12-18 lakh annually), while a two-year German public-university programme runs about Rs 22 lakh to Rs 28 lakh with minimal tuition and an 18-month post-study job window, and a one-year Irish master's ranges from Rs 28 lakh to Rs 42 lakh with up to 24 months of employment access under Stamp 1G. Consultant Mohammed Saqlain reported that the UK became the top preference for Telangana students in 2025-26 after issuing more than 95,000 study visas at a roughly 4 per cent rejection rate and offering two years of post-study work; Ireland enquiries rose about 45 per cent overall with student numbers from these states up nearly 50 per cent over two years in fields like data science and computer science; and New Zealand's Indian student population grew from 1,600 in 2022 to 13,000 by 2026 despite tightening approval rates to around 50-60 per cent. The article notes these figures are drawn from consultant estimates rather than official statistics, and cautions that students should evaluate accreditation, course quality, employment prospects, visa rules, and total costs before choosing a destination.
items.title: Telugu-State Students Shift from US to Europe Amid Tightened Visa Rules

items.summary: Police in Hyderabad placed two locations on high alert after receiving an email titled 'Lashkar-E-Taiba' addressed to senior police officials, including the Joint Commissioner of Police (Special Branch), which claimed affiliation with the group and threatened twin bomb blasts at Hotel Tourist Plaza in Kachiguda and Kachiguda Railway Station. The threat note warned of a possible attack on the lines of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks and alleged that the sender intended to kill a minimum of 300 people, framing it as retaliation for the killing of LeT militant Lateef Bhat by Indian Army forces in an encounter at Zangalpora, Kulgam district, on November 18. The letter described the threat as an urgent security concern and directed officials to strengthen surveillance and patrolling at the two named locations plus crowded public areas, hotels, railway stations, bus terminals, religious places, and other important establishments, while watching for suspicious individuals, unattended objects, vehicles, and unusual activities.
items.title: Hyderabad Police Sound High Alert After Alleged Lashkar-e-Taiba Threat

items.summary: Congress leader and Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi posted on X a picture of the Ardhanareeshwar sculpture at Elephanta Caves—depicting Shiva merged with Parvati—to accompany an attack on the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). In the caption, dated November 22, 2026, he characterized these organizations as "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists with absolutely no understanding of our spiritual and religious traditions." A separate post from November 17, 2026 framed his criticism around what he described as fear, anger, and hatred among BJP-RSS supporters that prevent them from experiencing love; he stated it is "his duty" as a Hindu to free them from these emotions so they can experience "the breathtaking beauty and joy of love and belonging." The report notes the comments followed earlier criticism Gandhi drew over remarks about his parents' relationship. It also reports an unrelated Saturday exchange in which Gandhi criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's questions on wage hikes and job creation, calling those remarks a confession of economic policy failures by the government. Attribution to ANI inputs is noted for the piece.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Attacks BJP-RSS Using Ardhanareeshwar Image
